newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked and unlinked bonds end higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked and unlinked bonds end higher.

text.p: Israeli inflation-linked and unlinked bonds closed higher on Wednesday, with traders saying the market has reached an equilibrium for the time being.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.06 pct to 172.4
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 pct to 162.52
Volume was moderate at 131 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds.

"CPI-linked bonds rose today because there are simply no sellers in the market. Institutional investors have stopped selling and therefore inflation-linked bonds are continuing to rise," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

"The market has reached an equilibrium. Yields on inflation-linked bonds are now around 4.4 percent, which is almost equal to the yields offered by unlinked bonds," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir of Ahrayut Investment Mangement.
Traders noted that yields on the Makam are now 14.5 percent. "With 1997 inflation expectations of 10 percent the yields are similar to those offered by CPI-linked bonds," Ben-Yaeir added.
"Unlinked bonds rose today because investors now believe that the government will meet its 1997 inflation target of seven to 10 percent," said Michael Weiss of Evergreen Capital Markets.
Dollar-linked bonds closed lower in response to the rise of the shekel against the dollar this week.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
